title: Longitudinal COM of trunk segments of living males by MRI

quantity.name: segment COM (longitudinal)
quantity.definition: CM position along segment long axis as % of segment length from the proximal (superior) end

source.authors: Pearsall DJ, Reid JG, Ross R
source.sample: 26 males; 26 living adult males, MRI (Philips 1.5 T), prone, arms above head; 10-mm slices every 50 mm
source.notes: height SD 5.7 cm; body mass SD 16.8 kg (range 56.4-129 kg); BMI 28.6 ± 4.8 (range 19.7-39.3). DOI not printed in PDF (likely 10.1007/BF02368294 – verify).

protocol.summary: Longitudinal CM positions of thorax, abdomen, pelvis and whole trunk (CMPC); trunk also as % of suprasternal notch–symphysis distance (CMPC*).
how_to_use: Place thorax/abdomen/pelvis COM at 51.5/49.0/44.7 % of each segment's length from its superior boundary.
Place whole-trunk COM at 53.0 % of the suprasternal notch–pubic symphysis distance from the notch.
Antero-posterior COM offsets are not given here; use Pearsall 1996 (CT) for COM anterior to vertebral centroids.

measurement.device: Philips Gyroscan 1.5 T; tissue densities assigned per pixel (cortical bone 1.8, cancellous 1.1, viscera/muscle/blood 1.06, adipose 0.96, lung 0.25 g/cc)

protocol.notes: Thorax = suprasternal notch (~T4/5) to xiphoid (~T9); abdomen = xiphoid to umbilicus (~L3/4); pelvis = umbilicus to pubic symphysis/greater trochanter (incl. perineum, excl. thighs); trunk = sum. Boundaries follow Zatsiorsky & Seluyanov gamma-scan definitions (thus close to de Leva UPT/MPT/LPT).

extraction.check_notes: Checked against rendered Table 1 (p.697). Trunk CMPC min 49.7 and max 46.4 are printed inverted/inconsistent with mean 48.0 – kept as printed.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
